questions.help: ALCOHOL AND OTHER DRUGS       16.1 Factors affecting alcohol limitsThe state of vigilance. Alcohol is eliminated more slowly when the person sleeps than when they are awake, so it is possible that if someone goes to sleep having consumed a large amount of alcohol, when they wake, they will, in addition to having a potential hangover, still be over the legal limit. Therefore, it may not be enough to sleep for a few hours and then drive. The following diagram demonstrates that the blood alcohol content begins to rise after the first drink, reaching an ultimate peak. It then shows the time it takes to reduce this level after having reached a maximum rate just over 2 g/l.The speed at which the drink is consumed. If consumption occurs over a period of time, the body may remove a portion of alcohol before receiving the next dose, thereby achieving the peak blood alcohol limit at a somewhat lower level than if the same amount of alcohol is taken in a shorter time.(Página 42 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help: ALCOHOL AND OTHER DRUGS       16.1 Factors affecting alcohol limitsThe time that has elapsed since the alcohol was consumed. It is possible to detect alcohol 5 minutes after consuming it. Over time this increases and a maximum is reached (called peak blood alcohol content) about an hour later. (Note: This may vary between 30 and 90 minutes) The level starts to fall below this maximum level very slowly with the effects lasting for    several hours and it will not completely disappear for a further period of time.The type of drink and method of ingestion. Alcohol is absorbed more quickly in distilled beverages (such as whiskey or gin) than through fermented drinks (such as beer or wine). In addition, hot drinks or carbonated drinks (fizzy ones such as tonics or other soft drinks) accelerate the absorption of alcohol.(Página 42 del manual 'Learning to drive')

cualquier usuario de la vía o conductor de vehículo.
any road user or vehicle driver.

cualquier usuario de la vía con síntomas de estar bajo sus efectos.
any road users appearing to be under the influence.

los conductores que sean denunciados por alguna infracción.
drivers who are reported for any violation.

questions.help: ALCOHOL AND OTHER DRUGS         18 Screening for blood alcohol or drugsIn order to detect this antisocial behaviour, tests to detect alcohol or drugs will be used. These tests are mandatory for:All road users or drivers of vehicles directly involved as possible persons responsible for a traffic accident.Any driver of a vehicle showing symptoms of being under the effects of these substances.(Página 45 del manual 'Learning to drive')ALCOHOL AND OTHER DRUGS     18.1 Tests to detect alcohol and drugs All drivers who have been reported for a traffic offence and other road users when they have committed an offence.All drivers who are requested to carry out a test at a police traffic control.Refusal to comply with the obligation to submit to an alcohol detection test or a drug detection test may result in the loss of 6 points.Refusal to do an alcohol detection test or a drug detection test is an offense publishable under the Criminal Code. (Página 45 del manual 'Learning to drive')
